title: Masterpieces
description: The most iconic paintings of all time — start here.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, Rijksmuseum, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Mona Lisa
items.description_narrative: The most famous painting in the world. It depicts Lisa Gherardini, wife of Francesco del Giocondo, sitting in front of an imaginary landscape. Her enigmatic expression and the masterful use of sfumato make it a masterpiece of the Renaissance.
items.tags: portrait, renaissance, sfumato, enigmatic, female
items.credit_line: C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition: image page

items.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura), also known as The Great Wave, from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei)"
items.description_narrative: Katsushika Hokusai's iconic color woodblock print, 'The Great Wave,' captures a colossal wave cresting over three fishing boats, threatening to engulf them amidst a turbulent sea. In the distance, the serene form of Mount Fuji stands against the sky, anchoring this dramatic scene from his famous series 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji.'
items.tags: great wave, mount fuji, ukiyo-e, woodblock print, ocean, dramatic, japanese landscape
items.credit_line: Library of Congress Catalog: https://lccn.loc.gov/2008660568 Image download: https://cdn.loc.gov/service/pnp/jpd/02000/02018v.jpg Original url: https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2008660568/

items.title: The Starry Night
items.description_narrative: A swirling, dynamic night sky over a quiet village, painted during Van Gogh's stay at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. It is one of the most recognized masterpieces in the history of Western art.
items.tags: night, sky, stars, village, post-impressionism, landscape

items.title: The Scream
items.medium: Oil, tempera, pastel and crayon on cardboard
items.description_narrative: An agonized figure against a tumultuous orange sky, standing on a bridge. Widely interpreted as representing the universal anxiety of modern humanity. Munch described the inspiration as feeling an infinite scream passing through nature.
items.tags: scream, anxiety, expressionism, bridge, sunset, anguish
items.credit_line: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

items.title: De Nachtwacht
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' depicts the company of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq and Lieutenant Willem van Ruytenburch moving out, renowned for its dramatic use of light and shadow. This monumental group portrait is a masterpiece of the Dutch Golden Age, celebrated for its dynamic composition and psychological depth.
items.tags: dutch golden age, group portrait, baroque, militia, dramatic, masterpiece, civic guard

items.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
items.description_narrative: Often referred to as the 'Mona Lisa of the North', this tronie depicts a European girl wearing an exotic dress, an oriental turban, and what appears to be a very large pearl as an earring. It is a masterclass in the use of light.
items.tags: portrait, dutch golden age, pearl, turban, female

items.title: Water Lilies
items.description_narrative: Claude Monet's 'Water Lilies' captures the ephemeral play of light and reflection on the surface of his water garden at Giverny. This painting is part of an extensive series, through which Monet explored the subtle changes in nature across different times of day and seasons.
items.tags: water lilies, pond, nature, impressionism, french art, tranquil, reflections, garden

items.title: The Creation of Adam
items.description_narrative: The most famous section of the Sistine Chapel ceiling. God reaches out to give life to Adam, their fingers nearly touching. This single gesture has become one of the most replicated religious images and an enduring icon of humanity.
items.tags: fresco, sistine chapel, genesis, god, adam, renaissance
items.credit_line: Own work Burkhard Mücke Taken on 18 October 2017

items.title: American Gothic
items.description_narrative: A stern-faced farmer standing beside his spinster daughter in front of a house with a distinctive Gothic window. One of the most familiar images in 20th-century American art, it is an ambiguous statement about rural American character.
items.tags: portrait, american, gothic, rural, farmer, pitchfork
items.credit_line: Art Institute of Chicago: online database: entry 6565

items.title: Sunflowers
items.description_narrative: One of two series of sunflower still lifes by Van Gogh. Painted in Arles to decorate the room of his friend Paul Gauguin, the vivid yellows and expressive brushwork make this among the most recognizable still-life paintings in art history.
items.tags: sunflowers, still life, yellow, vase, post-impressionism

items.title: The Birth of Venus
items.description_narrative: The goddess Venus emerges from the sea as a fully grown woman, arriving at the shore on a giant scallop shell. One of the world's most famous and appreciated works of art, it has become a landmark of Italian Renaissance painting.
items.tags: mythology, venus, renaissance, goddess, shell, classical

items.title: Nighthawks
items.description_narrative: Four figures sit in a brightly lit diner at night on a desolate city corner. The painting captures the loneliness and alienation of modern urban life with cinematic intensity. It has become one of the most reproduced paintings in American art.
items.tags: diner, night, urban, loneliness, realism, american

items.title: The Kiss
items.medium: Oil and gold leaf on canvas
items.description_narrative: A couple locked in an intimate embrace, cloaked in elaborate gold-patterned robes, kneeling in a flower-strewn meadow. Klimt's masterful use of gold leaf and ornamental motifs epitomizes his 'Golden Phase' and the height of the Vienna Secession movement.
items.tags: love, gold, art nouveau, couple, embrace, ornamental

items.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
items.description_narrative: Georges Seurat's monumental oil on canvas, "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884," captures Parisians enjoying a leisurely afternoon on an island in the Seine. This iconic work is meticulously composed using the artist's groundbreaking pointillist technique, creating luminous color and form.
items.tags: sunday, leisure, park, pointillism, post-impressionism, Parisian life, serene, vibrant

items.title: Café Terrace at Night
items.description_narrative: A warmly lit café terrace on the Place du Forum in Arles, France, under a deep blue starry sky. One of Van Gogh's first paintings to feature his signature nocturnal sky, it contrasts the warm golden gaslight with the cool blues of the evening.
items.tags: cafe, night, stars, arles, post-impressionism, urban

items.title: The School of Athens
items.description_narrative: A fresco in the Apostolic Palace in the Vatican depicting a congregation of the greatest philosophers, mathematicians, and scientists of antiquity, with Plato and Aristotle at the center. It is considered a masterpiece of perspective and one of the greatest achievements of Renaissance art.
items.tags: philosophy, plato, aristotle, fresco, renaissance, architecture
items.credit_line: "School of Athens" by Raphael, Raphael Rooms, Vatican Museum Complete indexed photo collection at WorldHistoryPics.com.

items.title: Ophelia
items.description_narrative: John Everett Millais's *Ophelia* vividly captures the tragic moment of Ophelia's drowning, as described in Shakespeare's *Hamlet*. The artwork is renowned for its meticulous detail in depicting the surrounding flora and Ophelia's ethereal pose, painted from a model floating in water.
items.tags: ophelia, shakespeare, pre-raphaelite, victorian art, tragedy, nature, detail, melancholy

items.title: Whistler's Mother
items.description_narrative: Formally titled 'Arrangement in Grey and Black No.1', this austere portrait of Whistler's mother seated in profile has become an American cultural icon and symbol of motherhood. Its restrained palette and compositional harmony exemplify Whistler's belief in art for art's sake.
items.tags: portrait, mother, seated, profile, tonalism, grey

items.title: Liberty Leading the People
items.description_narrative: Commemorating the July Revolution of 1830, the allegorical figure of Liberty strides over barricades and fallen fighters, holding the tricolour flag aloft. It combines the idealism of classical art with the gritty reality of modern war.
items.tags: revolution, liberty, flag, france, romanticism, battle
items.credit_line: Erich Lessing Culture and Fine Arts Archives via artsy.net

items.title: The Lady of Shalott
items.description_narrative: John William Waterhouse's iconic painting depicts the tragic Lady of Shalott from Tennyson's poem, captured at the moment she leaves her island tower to face her doom. Her gaze fixed towards Camelot, she sits in a boat amidst unraveling tapestry threads, embodying a pivotal moment of fate and consequence.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, victorian, painting, literature, arthurian legend, symbolism, tragic, romanticism
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — RQHFwa4u2LTw0g Tate Images (http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N01543&wwwflag=3&imagepos=2)

items.title: Impression, Sunrise
items.description_narrative: The painting that gave the Impressionist movement its name. A hazy sunrise over the port of Le Havre, rendered in loose, visible brushstrokes that prioritize the sensation of light and color over precise detail.
items.tags: sunrise, harbor, boats, impressionism, fog, water

items.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
items.description_narrative: A quintessential piece of Romanticism. A man stands upon a rocky precipice with his back to the viewer, gazing out over a landscape covered in a thick sea of fog. It evokes a feeling of the sublime and the profound scale of nature.
items.tags: fog, mountains, romanticism, sublime, landscape, wanderer

items.title: The Milkmaid
items.description_narrative: A kitchen maid carefully pours milk from a jug into an earthenware bowl, bathed in soft natural light from a window. Vermeer elevates an ordinary domestic scene into a meditation on quiet dignity and the beauty of everyday life.
items.tags: domestic, light, milk, kitchen, dutch golden age, still life
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — AHrw. Z3. Av6. Zhjg 9. AHrw. Z3. Av6. Zhjg

items.title: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
items.description_narrative: Manet's last major work depicts a barmaid at the famous Parisian cabaret, standing behind a marble counter laden with bottles. The mirror behind her reflects the bustling crowd. A brilliant study in modernity and the complex relationship between viewer and subject.
items.tags: bar, barmaid, mirror, paris, impressionism, nightlife

items.title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
items.description_narrative: This monumental work captures the dramatic moment when Jesus Christ calls Matthew to abandon his life as a tax collector and follow him. Caravaggio's use of intense chiaroscuro and naturalism illuminates the figures, highlighting the spiritual encounter within a seemingly everyday setting.
items.tags: religious, biblical, baroque, chiaroscuro, tenebrism, dramatic, naturalism, calling

items.title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
items.description_narrative: A vibrant depiction of a typical Sunday afternoon at the Moulin de la Galette in the Montmartre district of Paris. The dappled sunlight filtering through the trees onto the dancing crowd is one of Impressionism's most celebrated treatments of light and motion.
items.tags: dance, party, paris, montmartre, impressionism, sunlight

items.title: The Bedroom
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'The Bedroom' depicts his living space in the 'Yellow House' in Arles, France. The painting features vibrant colors and a distinctive perspective, inviting viewers into the artist's personal world.
items.tags: interior, bedroom, post-impressionism, vibrant, personal, arles
items.credit_line: rgHdFPzCeCfnxQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Flaming June
items.description_narrative: Frederic Leighton's iconic work depicts a woman in a vibrant orange gown, asleep in a dream-like, contorted pose. Bathed in the golden light of a setting sun, the figure is positioned against a distant, serene Mediterranean seascape.
items.tags: sleeping woman, aestheticism, victorian art, classical, mediterranean, orange, opulence, repose

items.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
items.description_narrative: Gustave Caillebotte's 'Paris Street; Rainy Day' captures a striking urban scene in 1877 Paris, depicting well-dressed figures strolling under umbrellas on a wet street. The composition offers a unique perspective of modern city life, characterized by its precise realism and distinctive viewpoints.
items.tags: urban life, street scene, rainy day, 19th century, realism, city, umbrellas, french art

items.title: Water Lily Pond
items.description_narrative: Claude Monet's "Water Lily Pond" captures the shimmering surface of the artist's garden pond at Giverny, a subject he repeatedly explored. Through vibrant brushstrokes, Monet meticulously renders the interplay of light, water, and vegetation, creating an immersive atmospheric effect.
items.tags: water lilies, pond, garden, impressionism, landscape, nature, serene, painting

items.title: The Slave Ship
items.description_narrative: J. M. W. Turner's 'The Slave Ship' vividly captures the raw power of the sea amidst a tumultuous sky. The painting dramatically illustrates the tragic practice of throwing enslaved individuals overboard, symbolizing the brutality of the slave trade.
items.tags: slavery, maritime, romanticism, sublime, abolition, tragedy, seascape, oil painting

items.title: Breezing Up (A Fair Wind)
items.description_narrative: This iconic American painting depicts four figures in a dory battling a choppy sea under a strong breeze. The dynamic composition and realistic portrayal capture the excitement and challenge of maritime life.
items.tags: sailing, marine art, American realism, dory, ocean, seascape
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: The Monk by the Sea
items.description_narrative: This iconic painting by Caspar David Friedrich depicts a small, solitary monk gazing out at a vast, turbulent sea under an expansive, dark sky. The stark contrast between the human figure and the overwhelming natural world evokes a profound sense of awe, isolation, and spiritual contemplation.
items.tags: landscape, romanticism, sublime, solitude, sea, contemplation, German art, melancholic

items.title: The Supper at Emmaus
items.description_narrative: Caravaggio powerfully depicts the dramatic moment Christ reveals himself to two disciples in Emmaus, capturing their astonished reactions. The artist masterfully employs intense chiaroscuro and lifelike figures, drawing the viewer into this profound biblical scene.
items.tags: religious, baroque, chiaroscuro, realism, dramatic, biblical, italian

items.title: Eight Bells
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'Eight Bells' depicts two sailors on a ship's deck, with one using a sextant to take an observation at sea. The artwork powerfully captures the forces of nature and the human endeavor against the ocean.
items.tags: marine art, realism, American art, seascape, maritime, sailors, observation, ocean
items.credit_line: 1. about.com2. Addison Gallery of American Art

items.title: The Icebergs
items.description_narrative: Frederic Edwin Church's monumental painting, "The Icebergs," presents a dramatic and detailed depiction of ice formations in the North Atlantic. The artwork captures the raw, sublime beauty and immense scale of nature, reflecting the artist's meticulous observation and grand artistic vision.
items.tags: landscape, arctic, icebergs, hudson river school, romanticism, sublime, american art, nature

items.title: Hylas and the Nymphs
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts the mythological youth Hylas being enticed by water nymphs, who emerge from a tranquil pool. Their captivating gazes and outstretched arms draw Hylas towards his tragic fate, as he was eventually drowned by them.
items.tags: greek mythology, nymphs, hylas, pre-raphaelite, oil painting, classical, alluring, tragic

items.title: The Conversion of Saint Paul on the Way to Damascus
items.description_narrative: This painting dramatically captures the moment Saul, en route to Damascus, is struck by a blinding light and hears the voice of Christ, leading to his conversion into Saint Paul. Caravaggio employs intense chiaroscuro and a stark composition to heighten the spiritual and physical impact of this divine intervention.
items.tags: religious, biblical, baroque, conversion, Paul, dramatic, chiaroscuro
items.credit_line: Web Gallery of Art: Image Info about artworkwga QS:P11807,"c/caravagg/05/29ceras"

items.title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
items.description_narrative: Caravaggio's painting dramatically captures the biblical story of Judith beheading the Assyrian general Holofernes. The artist employs intense chiaroscuro and stark realism to highlight the gruesome and harrowing nature of the act.
items.tags: biblical, Baroque, chiaroscuro, violence, drama, realism, Old Testament
